data.title: Ascent Sequences Avoiding Pairs of Patterns

data.inspection_scope: Propositions 6 and 10 with displayed arguments; Section 3 Dyck-path definition and encoding discussion
data.rights_note: Linked source and brief original extraction; no full text redistributed

data.review_note: Inspected statement and final-digit decomposition recurrence. Source review does not formalize the grammar/path bridge or alter the engine empty-word convention.

assumptions: Ordinary zero-based ascent sequences, equality-sensitive classical subsequence patterns 000 and 101.
This benchmark uses nonempty n>=1; the auxiliary Motzkin recurrence/grammar includes an empty object at degree zero.
data.indexing: degree n is word length; bridge comparison n>=1; source engine empty word excluded
data.pattern_semantics: Relative order and equalities of selected entries; no consecutive constraint
data.statement: The number of ordinary ascent sequences avoiding 000 and 101 is the Motzkin number M_n. The displayed proof uses deletion of a singly occurring final digit, or splitting around two final-digit copies, giving the Motzkin recurrence.
